page: Vultr vcg-a40-1c-5g-2vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family, designed for entry-level accelerated workloads. The server features a single dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 5.0 GB of system memory. Graphics acceleration is provided by a fractional partition of an NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, delivering 2 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 90 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear division between general-purpose compute and GPU-accelerated tasks. Due to the single-core configuration, multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and memory bandwidth fall into the lower percentiles. However, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities in specialized workloads. LLM inference benchmarks for a small 135M model reach top-tier status, delivering 9931.92 tokens per second for prompt processing and 454.57 tokens per second for text generation. Prompt processing for a medium 7B model also performs well, achieving 211.23 tokens per second.

This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient entry point for developers requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated card. The primary tradeoff is the limited single-core CPU capacity and 5.0 GB memory ceiling, which constrains heavy parallel processing and large-scale database hosting. It is best suited for lightweight LLM inference, small-scale model testing, batch text processing, and learning environments for CUDA-based development.

It is best suited for lightweight model deployment, text processing, and CUDA development.
